market_summary: Global markets recovered on US election day (November 5, 2026) amid a "AI rout" in recent trading, with major tech stocks including META and AAPL in focus as investors assessed Q3 earnings and AI spending plans. Singapore's key banks UOB and DBS reported Q3 results showing mixed performance amid margin pressures from funding costs. Meta raised $15 billion in bonds on November 3 as part of its massive AI infrastructure spending, joining other Big Tech companies in aggressive debt-funded capex plans. Apple reported record fiscal 2026 revenue of $478.8 billion with Q4 growth of 12%, though margin headwinds from rising memory costs emerged. Markets are navigating between growth opportunities and rising funding costs amid elevated interest rates.

items.headline: UOB Q3 2026 net profit S$1.25b misses forecast despite record fee income
items.summary: <cite index="1-2,1-5">UOB's Q3 net profit of S$1.25 billion fell 15% QoQ and missed the S$1.38 billion consensus forecast</cite>. <cite index="4-4">Net fee income surged 19% year-on-year to a record S$733 million, while wealth management fees reached a record S$258 million</cite>. <cite index="3-2">Trading and investment income slid 33% year-over-year</cite>.

items.headline: Meta raises $15 billion in bond sale to fund AI infrastructure expansion
items.summary: <cite index="22-9">Meta raised $15 billion through a five-part US dollar bond offering to finance accelerating investments in AI infrastructure</cite>. <cite index="22-14">Meta expects capital expenditure of $135 billion-$145 billion this year, largely driven by AI investments</cite>. <cite index="21-4,21-8">S&P Global Ratings revised the company's outlook from AA- stable to AA- negative, citing uncertainty about its heavy capex spending and negative free cash flow</cite>.

items.headline: Apple reports record fiscal 2026 revenue of $478.8B, Q4 growth 12% but faces margin pressure
items.summary: <cite index="45-6,45-14">Apple reported record revenues for fiscal 2026 of $478.8 billion, with revenue increasing 15% from $416.2 billion in fiscal 2025, while net income climbed 18% from $112 billion</cite>. <cite index="39-1,39-3">September quarter revenue reached $114.5 billion, up 12% year-over-year, with December quarter total revenue projected to grow 7% to 10%</cite>. <cite index="39-11">Rising memory chip prices are compressing hardware profitability, forcing price increases on Mac computers and iPad tablets</cite>.

items.headline: DBS Q3 2026 earnings due November 5, with analysts watching loan growth and margins
items.summary: <cite index="19-4,19-5">DBS's total income reached S$6.09 billion in Q2, up 6%, with net profit rising 9% to a record S$3.08 billion, ahead of the S$2.88 billion Bloomberg consensus</cite>. <cite index="19-7">DBS now expects 2026 total income to exceed 2025, and lifted its forecast for growth in commercial-book non-interest income to the mid-teens</cite>.

items.headline: OCBC Q3 2026 earnings scheduled for November 6, tracking record H1 2026 performance
items.summary: <cite index="33-6,33-7">OCBC entered Q3 on the back of its strongest-ever first half: S$4.19 billion net profit for 1H 2026, a 13% year-on-year improvement, with interim dividend of 47 cents per share declared</cite>. <cite index="33-9">Key items to watch on 6 November: NIM (already down ~25bp in 1H 2026), non-interest income momentum from Bank of Singapore, and any capital management announcements</cite>.

items.headline: Singapore Airlines passenger data breach: 46,000 booking records illegally accessed via Amadeus software
items.summary: Singapore Airlines disclosed that 46,000 booking records were illegally accessed in a data breach affecting software provider Amadeus's systems, compromising customer information stored in SIA's reservations.

items.headline: Google responds to backlash over removing search from schools that ban AI
items.summary: Google announced it is removing its search services from schools that ban AI tools, prompting political backlash and raising concerns about whether tech companies should be making such policy decisions in education.

items.headline: S&P 500 and Nasdaq recover from AI rout on US midterm election day
items.summary: Major equity indices recovered on November 5 as investors regained risk appetite on US election day, reversing earlier AI-related selloffs that had pressured tech stocks including META, AAPL, and other semiconductor-exposed names.
